correctness.rationale: Depth t decimations are constants, so at most 1+k+⋯+k^t distinct nodes; a period word with all symbols distinct attains it. Least period k^t forces a nonconstant depth-(t−1) chain whose t distinct ancestors cannot cycle because all depth≥t nodes are constants; plus two distinct constant outputs gives lower t+2. Interleave m≤k lower-exponent periodic child sequences with pairwise private nonzero symbols and shared 0: exact period multiplies k, and kernel rank is 2+Σ(q_j−1). For all except binary exponent-2 boundary, intervals I_m=[2+mt,2+m(B_{t−1}−1)] connect whenever B_{t−1}≥2t; direct base words 0001,0102,0012,0123 cover (2,2). Unsharing zeros among maximal children fills top k−1 ranks through B_t. Independent equality-pattern partition census confirms all intervals for (k,t)=(2,1),(2,2),(2,3),(3,1),(3,2), totaling 25,285 primitive patterns; finite enumeration is not the all-parameter proof.
residual_risks: Requires arbitrary finite alphabet; fails as stated if incorrectly interpreted as binary-only.

value.rationale: The set of attainable k-kernel ranks of a canonical noncoprime family is a natural exact automatic-sequence invariant. The proof determines both universal sharp endpoints and every intermediate possible value across all bases/exponents, with a nontrivial interleaving induction and exceptional binary boundary. The precision can support future automata complexity classifications independently of a more general mixed-period theory.
residual_risks: Alphabet size is unrestricted; fixed-alphabet rank spectrum remains outside the claim.

final_claim: For k≥2 and t≥1, the exact possible cardinalities of k-kernels of sequences with least period exactly k^t on arbitrary finite (size-unrestricted) alphabets are every integer from t+2 to (k^(t+1)−1)/(k−1), inclusive.
limitations: No fixed binary output alphabet, mixed coprime/noncoprime period, k-regular vector-space rank or MSDF-state-complexity conclusion. Finite census independently confirms examples, not the universal theorem.
